commit message:
[bert forward modeling] rework handling of contact impedances and
contact resistances for CEM electrodes:
	* add the setter function setContactResistances so we can
	  directly set electrode contact resistances from the Python
	  side
	* adding this function required slight changes in the internal
	  handling logic. Previously the code needed only to look for
	  contact impedances registered using the setter function, and thus it
	  was easier to decide which resistance type to actually use
          (contact impedances and contact resistances can be converted to each
          other if the electrode surface area is known). Now we solve this by an
          explicit parameter `use_cimp` which decides if the provided impedance
          (=true) or resistance (=false) vectors shall be used further.
	* setter functions are overwritten by input from files
	  contactImpedance.map and contactResistance.map.
	* resistance input always overwrites impedance input

commit message:
Update ertIPManager.py (#726)

In ERTIPManager I added the option to run a pure ERT inversion. I think this is useful to be able to make sure that the resistivity model is good before running the IP inversions. Before my change, this was not possible, because the invert() function in ERTIPManager was overwriting the invert() function in ERTManager, and there is no way of constructing an ERTIPManager object directly from an ERTManager object. Creating an invertDC function seemed to me the simplest solution...

This commit also includes test case for the issue.

Update ertIPManager.py

In ERTIPManager I added the option to run a pure ERT inversion. I think this is useful to be able to make sure that the resistivity model is good before running the IP inversions. Before my change, this was not possible, because the invert() function in ERTIPManager was overwriting the invert() function in ERTManager, and there is no way of constructing an ERTIPManager object directly from an ERTManager object. Creating an invertDC function seemed to me the simplest solution...

author: Anton Afanasyev <31539054+anstaf@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
iterate_domain related cleanup (#1106)

The major change: the contract for `iterator_domain` has been changed. Now it consists on two parts:
   - initialization and iteration over computation space is a subject of private contract between the given `iterator_domain` and the correspondent `execute_kernel`. It is backend specific.
  - the access to the data interface is backend independent. in the structured grid case it is a templated method `deref` that takes placeholder type and intent as a template (compile time only) parameters and accessor (from which only offsets are used) as a runtime parameters. Example:
```
   auto data_reference = it_domain. template deref<Arg, Accessor::intent>(accessor);
  // where accessor should be callable with `gridtools::accessor_offset` 
``` 
In other words: `iterator_domain` doesn't have to support the contract for the `Do` function `Evaluator` parameter.

This change illuminates the need of accessor remapping.

Minor changes:
- `bypass` and `IJK` cache types go away
- `is_texture_type` is rewritten using `meta` `API`
- `remove_qualifiers` goes away
- accessor predicates definitions moved to correspondent accessor definitions. unused accessor predicates are removed
- `stencils-functions API` now uses `Do` function `Evaluator` parameter public contract  instead of  `interator_domain` internal contract.

commit message:
Bugfix: return type in call (GC-454, #908)

Description: This is an addition to the fix in #882 where the `accessor_return_type` was fixed for `call_proc`. This fix revealed a similar issue in the `call`.
Our (arbitrary) convention was, that the return type of a `call` is the type of the first `inout_accessor` of the caller. However the implementation was wrong and this behavior cannot easily be fixed. Therefore this PR introduces a new convention (which is still arbitrary) to use the type of the first argument passed to the function.

API changes: Return type of `call` is the type of the first argument in the call. Additionally, the return type can be specified by `call:return_type<MyReturnType>::with(...)`.

Fixes for CUDA 9.2 (GCC-489, #977)

Description: Fixes issues with CUDA 9.2 compilation.

Details:
- CUDA9.2 doesn't like some parts of boost::fusion resulting in `convert_iterator.hpp(57): error: identifier "" is undefined in device code`. The fix is to replace these parts by std::tuple.
- tuple_util::apply was added (without support for invoking on member functions)
- permute_to was rewritten using tuples
- CUDA9.2 doesn't like boost::optional in its standard implementation. For version exactly 9.2 we enable the "old" optional implementation.

Issues: The code compiles fine on my computer with CUDA 9.2 but some tests fail at runtime, while they work (with these changes and the boost::optional workaround) with CUDA 8.0.

author: crosetto <crosetto@lifev.org>
commit message:
Replace operator! by global accessor (GC-67, #563, #495)

Feature description: Having storages which are global to the whole iteration space, and being able to access them from whithin the user functor with the operator(), was something achieved by prefixing an operator! to the accessor. Since there are no use cases for this when we access regular storages, and since this feature is used only for special storages which are always accessed using "global" indices, now the global_accessor is used instead of the operator().
The syntax changes because now instead of using a regular accessor we have to use a global_accessor, and there's no need anymore for the operator!, because the type of accessor is different. Fixes #495.

Detailed description:
A new type global_accessor_with_arguments is available (invisible to the user). There is an overload for operator() in the iterate_domain, so that it can be called from the Do method passing global indices like a storage (see example extended_4D for an example).

Additional changes:
Simplified the expressions metafunctions

commit message:
Introduce sid::composite and friends

Adding more of `SID` calculus stuff:
 - `sid::composite` models both `SID` and `tuple_like` concepts. Encapsulates the complexity of iterating several data storages together. Utilise `strides kind`s and `bounds validator kind`s.
- `sid::synthetic` provides a way of building custom storages from scratch
- `sid::delegate` a helper for implementing delegate  design pattern fo `SID`s
- `sid::clone` convert a `SID` to another `SID` that is trivially copyable

Several fixes to the previously introduced bugs:
- `tuple` : now tuple of tuples of empty objects are supported correctly
- `tuple_util`: 
  -`traits::getter`, `traits::to_types` `traits::from_types` are now `SFINAE` friendly also for compilers with broken template aliases
  - fix `fold` algorithm performance
  - fix compilation problems with `CUDA 8`
- several minor problems was fixed in `SID` concept API    

Addings to the underlined components:
 - `meta`:
   - `find` - find the first position of a type within a type list
   -  map operations: `mp_insert`, `mp_remove`, `mp_inverse`
   - `GT_META_PRINT_TYPE` and `GT_META_PRINT_VALUE` macros for compile time debugging
   - `iseq_to_list` and `make_idices` accept additional optional parameter which tells how to listify  
- `tuple_util`:
   - helper macros for propagating `tuple_like`-ness from the from the member
   - lazy variation of `element` metafunction
   - `all_of` algorithm
- `SID` concept API
  - concept defaults are exposed now under `default_strides`,`default_bounds_validator` etc. names
  - functor versions of concept runtime functions are exposed   
  
`SID` tests moved to its own subdirectory

commit message:
StencilCompiler unregisters invalid stencils

* When a stencil is run and the analyze() method from the compiler raises an exception for detecting an error, the stencil is unregistered from the compiler.
This ensures that when using a non-Python backend the compiler does not try to compile a stencil for which the code could not be generated, resulting in a failure of the build process for the whole library.

* Added EmptyKernelTest, a class to test if an empty kernel correctly raises analyzer errors and gets its stencil unregistered from the compiler.

* The stencil with the empty kernel has been extracted from the commented-out body of test_kernel_function() in test_stencils.py. This test contained obsolete code and has been removed, its purpose being effectively fulfilled by EmptyKernelTest.

* EmptyKernelTest can also serve as a base class to test other stencils with more complicated invalid kernels (usually kernels containing unsupported language features).

commit message:
New storage module (#577)

Feature description: Replace the storage module in gridtools. Fixes #448, fixes #394, fixes #339, fixes #279, fixes #278, fixes #291, fixes #320, fixes #314, fixes #308.

List of concepts:
1. storage: Internal storage backend (e.g., host_storage, cuda_storage, etc.).
2. storage_info: meta information about the storage (halo, alignment, size, etc.).
3. data_store: data_store can be seen as the element that is coupling together the storage_info and a data type. Acts like a shared_ptr to a storage and storage_info. This means it can be passed around and cleaned up in an easy way.
4. data store field is a collection of data_stores (of the same type).
5. view provides means to modify the data stored in a data_store or data_store_field.
6. storage-facility: The storage facility is used to get the correct types for the storage_info, data_store, data_store_field. The user (this is also predefined in the backend) passes the backend type (e.g., Cuda, Host) and can then use this storage facility to retrieve the proper types (e.g., cuda_storage_info in case of Cuda backend).

Details: The old storage contained many good concepts but still though the module was missing some features and had several design flaws that were fixed. List of internal changes:
1. Temporary flag for args.
2. Intermediate constructs and maintains a list of views instead of raw pointers.
3. Intermediate contains a copy of the aggregator and not a reference.
4. data stores and data store fields are synchronized automatically (when calling run) if in a non synchronized state.
5. Temporary allocation is now grid, backend, and execution strategy dependent
6. Iterate domain is not using a flattened list of pointers anymore but a type hierarchy that can be queried like the strides_cache.
7. Field offset calculation in iterate_domain is now different.
8. Temporaries are always aligned now (for all CUDA blocks).

Performance changes: Performance changed a little bit. Some structured grid test cases perform better now (e.g., vertical_advection, horizontal_diffusion, etc.). No performance changes when using icosahedral grids.

API changes: Following changes are the main API changes that affect the user.
1. The aggregator type construction is now done without passing pointers (aggregator_type<mpl_vec> domain(&in, &out); changed to aggregator_type<mpl_vec> domain(in, out);) but directly passing the storages.
2. There is no need to define temporary storages anymore. Instead we use tmp_arg<Id, StorageType> instead of arg<Id, StorageType>.
3. In order to modify the data contained in a data_store, or data_store_field the user has to create a view.
4. Synchronization can be done either with sync(). This method decides automatically what to sync. Otherwise the user can force synchronization with the former methods (clone_to_device(), clone_from_device()).

commit message:
Communication: Fix leak in MPI communicators (#1033)

Description: There was a leak problem with MPI communicators. The Halo update pattern did not clean up at destruction, and this was because we were copying communicators that were created somewhere else. Since MPI implementations has a limited number of communicators that they can handle, poor implementations of user code could exhaust them, or destroy communicators before their last use. For this reason, we needed to deprecate the constructors of the halo-update pattern that build communicators, and do a better job at freeing communicators.

API change: This has the implication that the communicator given to the distributed boundaries has to be a Cartesian communicator.

commit message:
Abstract reassign domain in aggregator (GC-225, #725)

Feature description: Enables possibility to use of reassign domain in cases were type erasure is needed.

Details: With the previous implementation of the reassign domain the full type of the computation has to be retained. This is not practical for large codes as compile time would explode (the type would need to be in a header and would be compiled for every translation unit).
The solution in this PR is to partly type-erase such that the placeholders are kept and the reassign works on this partly type-erased. The fully type-erased structs are called stencil and reduction (former computation) and the new partly type-erased struct is computation<Aggregator, ReductionType>.

API changes: Additional overload of run() which accepts parameters with the same interface as reassign (as a short-cut for reassign() + run()), i.e. either just a complete ordered list of storages or arg-storage pairs (only storages which should be reassigned).

Cleanup boost defines in CMake (GC-295, #774)

Description: `BOOST_NO_CXX11_DECLTYPE` and `BOOST_NO_CXX11_RVALUE_REFERENCES` defines are removed. BOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 is defined conditionally if CUDA version is 7. Fixes #748.

Additional changes: It turned out that `data_ptr_fusion_map` was defined as boost fusion map to C-array of pointers. Fusion map requires value_type to be passable as a return value to function. To fix compilation, C-arrays were replaced by `gridtools::array`s.

author: Anton Afanasyev <31539054+anstaf@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Use SID Strides (GC-564, #1205)

Description: Replaces use of storage_info by SID strides in stencil-composition.

Details:
- `local_domain` now holds the `hymap` from `storage_info` to `sid strides` instead of fusion vector of pointers to `storage_info`
important side effects:
- the strides are now in constant memory for cuda backend
- offset computations are performed via `sid::shift`
- cuda backend doesn't leak `storage_info`s anymore  

Performance changes:
- x86: small performance improvements on daint, tiny regression on kesch, tiny mixed result on tave
- cuda: daint: significant improvements for several stencils, significant regression for "Simple Horizontal Diffusion"; kesch: significant improvement on all stencils in float, mixed results (significant) in double
- mc: regression with (the officially not supported) icc

Additionally the cuda target was tested on the COSMO dycore stencils with the following result (weighted summed stencil time):
- V100: improvement between 1% and 6% (float/double, 129/257 domains)
- K80: improvement of 4% (float, 129/257 domains)
- P100: (float) regression for 129x129x80 domain of 2%, improvement of 2% for 257x257x80 domain

Fixes #1091, fixes #652.

This improves the behavior of hugepage_alloc in several ways (fixes #1561):
- Fixed hardcoded values: queries architecture-dependent L1 cache line size and set size at run time (Linux only).
- More conservative offsetting: makes sure that each cache set is considered.
- Explicit control over huge page allocation: introduces the environment variable GT_HUGEPAGE_MODE that can be used to switch between explicit huge page allocation, use of transparent huge pages and disabling huge pages (Linux only).

Refactoring: regression tests (GC-544, #1060)

Description: Reduce code duplications in the regression tests.

Details:
- `backend_select.hpp` deduplicated and moved to `include/gridtools/tools`
- `gtest` fixtures `computation_fixture` and `regression_fixture` are introduced; `regression_fixture` provides support for command line parameters and benchmarks and goes with the corresponding library (that contains `main` entry point); `computation_fixture` is header only
- `common/binops.hpp` upgraded to do proper perfect forwarding and `constexpr`
- `plh::operator=` is made `const`
- the `icc` version of `accessor` is fixed to support default offsets (as the regular version does)
- `explicit` was removed from `storage_info` constructors, which reduce the boilerplate around data storages creation.
- all `strgrid` binaries from `regression` that dealt with `Options.cpp` are rewritten to use `regression_fixture`
- `Options.*` and `benchmark.hpp` are used only for `icgrid` build; they are moved to the correspondent folder
- `horisontal_diffusion` and `vertical_advection` repositories are refactored in a way that they don't use anything `gridtools` specific (namely they don't use storage API)
- in `regression/icosahedral` unused benchmark code is removed from `lap` and `stencil_fused`
- some orphane files are deleted:
  - `regression/icosahedral/stencil_nested_on.*`
  - `regression/performance_baseline.org`
  - `regression/runTest_daint.job`
  - `regression/shallow_water_test.hpp`
- `icosahedral_topology::make_storage` implementation is simplified

Performance changes:

author: crosetto <crosetto@lifev.org>
commit message:
Allowing the expand_factor to be larger than the expandable parameter size (GC-122, #576, )

Feature description: The case in which a user defined an expandable parameters vector is smaller than the compile-time expand_factor value was considered an error (because there is no performance benefit in using expandable parameters in such cases). However this constraint has been relaxed, since the parameters length is a runtime parameter and may end up being less than the expand factor. In the latter case the execution happens as if the computation was replicated several times.

Detailed description:
If the parameters vector is larger than the expand_factor, then I need the m_intermediate, which contains the chunk of storages, so I instantiate it. If the size of the parameters vector is not divided exactly by the expand_factor, then I need also the m_intermediate_remainder, and I instantiate it as well (otherwise it doesn't get instantiated). Now if I allow the parameters vector to be smaller than the expand_factor, then I don't need to instantiate the m_intermediate, because I'll always use the m_intermediate_remainder. That's what these new "if" in intermediate_expand.hpp do. In the latter case the m_intermediate unique_ptr is left NULL.

commit message:
Loop Blocking for fn GPU Backend (#1787)

Implements loop blocking for the GPU fn backend. Thread block size (that
is, CUDA/HIP threads per block) and loop block size (that is, loop
iterations per CUDA/HIP thread) can now be specified as template
parameters.

Further changes:
- Set `__launch_bounds__` in the fn GPU kernel based on the thread block
size.
- Activate vertical loop blocking in the fn nabla kernels on newer CUDA
versions that support `GT_PROMISE`.

Performance changes:
- `__launch_bounds__` affects performance of the
`fn_cartesian_vertical_advection` benchmark significantly (positively or
negatively, depending on domain size).
- Performance of fn nabla benchmarks improves significantly on newer
CUDA versions.
- Performance on Daint is currently reduced due to too old CUDA version.

commit message:
Implement kparallel for CUDA backend (GC-490, #983)

Description: For the CUDA backend, kparallel execution policy splits the vertical axis among multiple blocks.

Details:
- The vertical dimension is split among blocks, such that each block processes a compile-time fixed number of layers.
- The kparallel execution policy is incompatible with kcaches.

Performance changes:
- Improves performance for the stencils which use the CUDA backend and kparallel execution policy, namely copy stencil and horizontal diffusion stencils.
- Stencils which use the CUDA backend and forward or backward execution policy show minor changes in performance (some of them slightly faster, some of them slightly slower).
- No changes for host backend.
- Minor changes for mic backend (probably independent from this PR).

commit message:
Use tuple_util to access accessor offset (#1212)

Details:
- `take` and `insert` algorithms are added to `meta`
- array tuple util getter is moved out of array class to reduce the number of instantiations
-  removed unused `unzip.hpp`
- removed unused `get_from_variadic_pack`
- `insert` algorithm is added to `tuple_util`
- accessors (including global) now model `tuple-like` and `hymap` concepts.
- `stencil_functions` are rewritten using tuple_util.
- removed unused `storage_info_extender`

API changes:

- `stencil_functions.hpp` moved one level up, i.e. `<gridtools/stencil_composition/stencil_functions.hpp>`

Performance changes:

 - Performance regression for horizontal diffusion fused with ICC and gcc. ICC is no longer supported as a well-performing compiler. gcc should be upgraded to version 6+ which restores the performance of this stencil. However the pyutils used for performance testing, currently don't support a different gcc for cuda and x86/mc compilation; CUDA doesn't work with gcc 6.

commit message:
Fixed a symbol shadowing bug

If a stage function parameter had the same name of the stencil scope's data field passed as argument (e.g. foo(in_data=in_data) ), the resulting stage alias symbol would have been resolved as pointing to itself, therefore preventing the detection of the real parameter value.
This compromised many other aspects of stencil analysis (data dependency, access pattern detection, halo detection, etc.)

Also removed a redundant if condition in Scope.add_parameter()

commit message:
Ptrs in const memory (GC-498, #982)

Description: For the CUDA backend data ptrs should be stored in local memory, not in shared memory.

Details:
- Originally ptrs were in global memory, therefore the optimization (copying to shared) was meaningful. In the meantime, the ptrs are already passed via const memory (as kernel parameters), therefore accessing them directly from the local_domain makes sense.
- This made a dispatching step to the backend obsolete.
- `mic` had offsets for data ptrs for temporaries. Now these offsets are stored (instead of the ptrs + offset).
- shared code `get_data_pointer()` moved to iterate_domain_aux

Performance changes:
Improved for CUDA structured grids for all stencils except:
- kesch-float-hdiff-fused-256
- kesch-double-advectionpdbott-256
- daint-double-copy-256
Small changes in CUDA icgrid
No changes for HOST
Minor changes for MIC

commit message:
CMake refactoring: modularization (GC-526, #1032)

Description: This PR is the first step in refactoring CMake files to allow for exporting of targets and custom installations. Fixes #1034, fixes #961.

Details: The first change is to use CUDA as a language, so that the same commands can be used for C++ targets and CUDA targets. This feature is still quite new in the CMake world and required quite some smithing, but should improve with new versions on CMake.
The second change was the ability to install only certain components, that is copy only the sources and libraries of, and run only the tests for, the components that the user decide to get. This does not incorporate a full featured export, but it's a first step.

Additional changes: I introduced here the test manifest, a file in the build folder, like the install-manifest, that lists all the tests executed when making GridTools. This file can be used to compare branches, to see if they run the same tests, which turned useful to find several bugs in my branch, and in master, too.

author: Felix Thaler <thaler@cscs.ch>
commit message:
Fix for Integer Format Check in Python SID Adapter (#1632)

Python integer format char is ambiguous and platform dependent. PyBind11 `format_descriptor<...>::format()` always returns "q" and "Q" for 64bit integers, independent of the platform. Compatible passed-in Python buffers on the other hand might also have the equivalent format "l" or "L" set. See https://github.com/pybind/pybind11/issues/1806 and https://github.com/pybind/pybind11/issues/1908 for details. This fix introduces a special case for integer format comparisons, just checking size and signedness.

commit message:
Fix vertical size of temporaries (#490, GC-14)

Bug description: To determine the k size of temporaries the value of the last splitter was used (the function value_at_top() was used to retrieve this value). The offsets in the k interval where not taken into account. 

Solution: Replace the value_at_top call by a function that calculates the size of the k interval. I decided to keep the change small and use the axis to determine the size in the new function k_total_length.

Drawback: The allocated size of the temporaries might be too large if the size of the axis does not match the size of the intervals in the computation, see #491.

Additional changes:
* removed value_at_top and value_at_bottom as its intention was not really clear to me (it returned the value first and last value of the value_list).
* replaced them by k_max and k_min which calculate the first and last k level by taking into account the axis offsets
* removed code duplication between common_grids/grid_cg.hpp and structured_grids/grid.hpp, moved most of the code to the base class.
* removed the grid ctor which was taking a gridtools::array (was only used once in structured_grids) and added a delegating ctor in icgrid to be removed later.
* rename common_grids/grid_cg.hpp to grid_base.hpp following the usual pattern.

Performance changes:
* In the refactoring the partitioner was moved to the base class leading to an increase in size of the grid in icosahedral. This resulted in a performance loss of ~5 % for one of the stencils. See issue #524. We accepted the loss for now as the partitioner belongs to the base class (if it belongs to the grid at all) and the performance loss is only for one stencil.

commit message:
Introduce dump backend  (#1546)

Stencil `dump` backend is added. It doesn't perform calculations. Instead it outputs `JSON` representation of the spec (the type that is passed to the backend entry point). Unlike other backends `dump` is stateful -- it contains the reference to the `std::ostream` that is served as an output sink. The usage is like that:
 ```
  run(fe_spec, dump{std::cout}, ...);
```
The context of this PR is the following: It is a step to extract the cosmo dycore model from the gt2 based source and to pass it into gt4py in the future. The main showstopper on this way is the fact that the elementary stencils are represented in the generated `json` as `C++` demangled type names. The next step could be to parse the sources with the python based tool and to extract the AST's from the stencil bodies.

Move to standalone c_bindings: cpp_bindgen (#1319)

Removes the c_bindings from the repository and re-includes cpp_bindgen via `FetchContent()` in a backward-compatible name (i.e. wrappers for the old names). These wrappers are deprectated and will be removed in GridTools 2.0.

Users should not notice this change except for a small detail: previously users exported the GridTools c_bindings CMake targets (e.g. handle) with the explicit name, now the new CMake function `install_cpp_bindgen_targets()` should be used to avoid this problem in the future.

New users should avoid using the cpp_bindgen provided with the GridTools CMake, but should explicitly use the standalone version from [GridTools/cpp_bindgen](https://github.com/GridTools/cpp_bindgen).

commit message:
API for K-caches  (GC-4, #536)

Feature description: Provide an API to support k caches and prepare all the code so that a accessing a cached field will be dispatched to specialized methods in the iterate domain cuda. Since full implementation of the k cache is not provided, this specialized method will simply resolve an access to gmem.  

Details:
- Remove protection that all output args should have null extent (it was too strict). Now we only check that the IJ components of the extent of an output arg are null. 
- The API of the cache is modified so that it supports now passing an Interval (only valid if using kcaches and no local io policy).
- A new method in the iterate domain cuda resolves accesses when the arg is being kcached. At the moment it points to gmem, since there is not actual implementation of kcaches

Additional changes:
- Adding a unittest for iterate domain cuda, in order to test the metafunctions that dispatch the accesses to the right memory type, e.g. accessor_from_kcache_reg. Now we can also test this and the "old" metafunctions that dispatch to texture memory.

commit message:
Hybercube iteration (GC-329, #862)

Description: Introduces a hypercube_view which allows to iterate over the positions of a N-dimensional hypercube, with `for(auto&& pos: make_hypercube_view(...) ...` which works on host and on device.

Details:
make_hypercube_view can be constructed
- from an array of pairs, where the pairs define the range to iterate in each dimension (end-point is excluded
- from an array of end-points (integers), the iteration range is from 0 to the (excluded) end-point.
E.g. `make_hypercube_view(make_array(make_pair(a,b),make_pair(c,d))`.

Other changes:
- added metafunction to convert the type of an array or to convert a tuple/pair to and array: convert_to_array<NewType>(array/tuple/pair).
- added metafunction to transpose and array<array<T,InnerD>,OuterD> to array<array<T,OuterD>,InnerD>
- the verifier was simplified to use this iterator
- pair and array more std-compliant: added tuple_element<>, get<>(), etc.
- copy_stencil test was broken (would never trigger), should be refactored to use the verifier
- fixed a problem with the k-axis in an example

commit message:
Expression unit tests (#708)

Bug description: Expression were lacking a unit test and some expressions were broken. Due to a bug in CUDA < 8 expressions are only fully supported with CUDA8. Fixes #419

Solution:
- Fixes the following expression: -arg (negate), +arg, float-arg, float/arg and combinations of args with integral types.
- Add unit tests (some disabled for CUDA < 8).

Additional changes:
Introduces a gtest addon which allows to write CUDA_TEST to generate a test for host and a test for device. The code in the test body is executed in a kernel. Values which are inside a ASSERT_EQ and ASSERT_FLOAT_EQ are copied back to host and compared there. All other ASSERTS and EXPECTS are not supported. Only bool, int and float is supported as values to be compared.

commit message:
Raise exception if stencil data field depends on itself

According to gridtools' data dependency rules, we cannot write into a field that is accessed in an extent different than <0,0> (1D) in a previous stage.
Thus, a field cannot depend on itself if its access extent is different from <0,0> in all dimensions.

This commit adds a StencilScope method to check data dependencies. It should be called after Stencil.generate_code(), when all data dependencies have been resolved at stencil's scope.
For the time being, no kind of self-dependency is supported.

commit message:
Convention for storage size and view.operator()(...) (GC-229, #688)

Feature description: operator()(0,0,0) points to first grid point in halo. The halo is kept in the storage_info type but it does not extend the storage anymore. The sizes that are passed to the storage info constructor must include the halo. 

API changes: Additionally to the dim, unaligned_dim, stride, unaligned_stride following new methods were added to the storage_info class:
1. begin: index of first non-halo data point
2. end: index of last non-halo data point
3. length: number of data points (excludes padding, halo, etc.)
4. total_begin: index of first halo point
5. total_end: index of last halo point
6. total_length: number of data+halo points (excludes padding)
7. padded_total_length: total length of the storage (halo, data, padding, initial offset)

author: Anton Afanasyev <31539054+anstaf@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Cleanup as a Part of Tmp Redesign (GC-486)

No user facing changes
-----------------------

- remove unused `fusion_vector_check_bound.hpp`
- add `reverse` algorithm to `meta`
- remove unused `reversed_range.hpp`
- remove unused `variadic_assert.hpp`
- `iterate_domain` templates now are not specified in `backend_traits` and `run_functor_arguments`, but instantiated directly in the corresponded execution kernel
- `positional_iterate_domain` now takes base `iterate_domain` class as an template parameter instead of CRTP base
- `is_positional_iterate_domain` now is implemented as a proper concept check
- remove CRTP base template parameter from `iterate_domain_*` template
- `iterate_domain` templates accept `RunFunctorArguments` template parameter directly instead of  deducing it from derived class
- `run_esf_functor` now is not selected via `backend_traits` but passed directly in the correspondent execution kernel
- `run_esf_functor` design is redone to avoid CRTP
- `tmp_storage API` now accepts the full `max extent` specification instead of `max_extent` only in `i` direction
- `k_loop` machinery is simplified by excluding CRTP pattern
- `storage_wrapper` was substituted by `arg` everywhere
- `make_stage` uses `std::tuple` instead of `mpl::vector` for the arguments list
- `mss_local_domain` RIP -- it contained from a single `mpl::vector` of `local_domain` of the size 1. Now `local_domain` is used instead everywhere.
- remove unused `total_storages.hpp`

There are several minor performance improvements here and there and no performance degradations.

commit message:
Reimplement Expandable Parameters (#1004)

- expandable parameters are now implemented by transforming to the real expanded versions of the mss descriptors. I.e. if mss had one stencil with expandable `arg`s and expand factor is `3`, for each expandable `arg`, three distinct new `arg`s will be generated. and mss will contain three `esf_descriptor`s [strictly speaking it will be one `independent_esf` with three esfs inside ] with the same functor, but with different sets of `arg`s. the expanded specs are passed to the regular `intermediate` which is now doesn't hold any expand factor and doesn't do anything specific to expandable parameters. 
- `arg` implementation is modified a bit: now `gridtools::arg` is just an alias of anothe struct called  `plh` which is not a part of user API and hold a tag, instead an integer as an unique ID.
- the direct support of the `data_storage_filed` is removed from the stencil_computaion API. Now only `data_store`es  and `std::vector`s of `data_store`es can be bound to placeholders. A single example the used this feature [shallow_water_enhanced] is modified to use `data_store`s directly.
- `vector_accesor` is going away. Now the plain `accessor` can be used instead.
- `define_caches` is simplified and now produces std::tuple instead of `mpl::vector`
- unimplemented `staggered API` is removed

commit message:
Redo gridtools::tuple (#1088)

- `get`/`tuple_element`/`tuple_size`, comparision operators (namely `==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=` and `>=` )  etc. are not implemented. Instead `tuple` is adopted to use with tuple_util library.
- `allocator` aware constructors are not implemented
- all constructors are implicit. [which violates the Standard]
- element wise direct constructor is not sfinae friendly
- encapsulation is compromised over simplicity. In particular `tuple` has public inheritance from its `impl`.
- all methods declared as noexcept [which violates the Standard]
- `swap` is implemented as a `__host__` function because it can call `std::swap`

commit message:
Check that compute domain is not empty (GC-107, #602, #555)

Bug description: The user could specify a grid with an empty compute domain which resulted in a run-time CUDA error. Fixes #555.

Solution: On construction of the halo_descriptor the values are checked for consistency. Throws an exception in case of wrong combination.

Additional changes:
- Adds a macro ASSERT_OR_THROW(cond, msg) which throws on host and asserts on device (CUDA > 8).
- Refactor: Remove setters in halo_descriptor as they were rarely used and the halo_descriptor might easily end up in  an invalid state. Replace the calls to set_minus(0) and set_plus(0) by reset_minus() and reset_plus() which were the only uses of the setters.
- Refactor: Replace if's by switch to make it uniform with similar pattern in other functions of the halo_descriptor.
- Refactor: Default constructor for halo_descriptor initializes total_length=1 instead of 0, because 0 would be an invalid state.
- Refactor: Delete duplicated halo_descriptor in communication.
- Some invalid halo_descriptors in unit_tests fixed.

author: Ioannis Magkanaris <iomagkanaris@gmail.com>
commit message:
Fix Clang warning with __builtin_assume (#1788)

Building the project with `Clang` generates the following warning:
```
the argument to '__builtin_assume' has side effects that will be discarded [-Wassume]
```

Seems like Clang doesn't handle the hint well unless we pass a
const/pure attribute to the function call inside the assume. See:
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/55636 and
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/93077

With this change performance for the fn fused nabla examples is
significantly improved on clang-cuda and is now much faster than (our
old) nvcc, which doesn't have `assume` support.

commit message:
Icosahedral backend with caches and fusion (GC-29, #550)

Feature description: Large new set of DSL syntax, and main performance optimizations to enable the mss fusion in CPU (esf fusion in CUDA) and IJ caches for icosahedral grids.

Details on new syntax:
- on_cells, ... with multiple (more than one) parameters passed to the lambda
- Accept user functor with a Color template parameter so that the user can customize the operation according to the color (downward or upward triangles)
- Assume order of neighbors in the icosahedral topology as part of the API. Some user operators might use a sign convention for the fluxes that will rely in this order of neighbors, therefore it should not be changed.
- Provide access to user functor to full connectivity table of the icosahedral topology.

Details on performance:
- strgrid: no changes
- icgrid: In the gpu several bugs were fixed which resulted in a significant improvement of the GPU performance. In CPU, examples are still vectorizing, so same performance is retained.

Additional changes:

- arg contains now a location type, which was required by irregular grids. But since could be used in the future for structured grids, and in order to still shared the same type, the location type was also added to structured grids but with a default null type (at the moment)
- Large set of new icosahedral examples to demonstrate the new syntax of the DSL
- Several new unittests

commit message:
Linking issue in clonable_to_gpu (GC-102, #610, #447)

Bug description: Classes inheriting from clonable_to_gpu have different members (the CUDA version has an extra gpu ptr) and therefore different sizes when compiled with nvcc or a host compiler. However, it is possible to link these two objects together without error since the symbols are identical. This will result in weird runtime errors. Fixes #447.

Solution: The solution is to compile clonable to gpu objects in the gpu code, and declare the object as extern in the host source. Then the symbol is resolved at linking time correctly.

author: cosunae <carlos.osuna@meteoswiss.ch>
commit message:
Redesign of the accessor (#545,GC-97)

Bug Description: Together with the expandable parameters functionality, the accessor saw a redesign that was difficult to read and follow due to a complex hierarchical design and hidden features
The current design looks like

accessor : accessor_mixed< accessor_impl<...> > : accessor_base

so that a "normal" accessor became a degenerated case of an accessor. At first sight, this seemed to be required in order to equip the normal accessor with a

template<ushort_t I> int get_constexpr()

However since the accessor_mixed used to build the degenerated accessor does not contain any <Pair...>,
any use of get_constexpr() should trigger a compile time error. In practice it does not trigger any error, since the accessor_mixed builds a non empty offset_tuple_mixed, non initialized, but constexpr. So it returns always 0 to any call to get_constexpr(). This is the hidden feature that I try to make here more explicit by:

1) recovering the old design, that is more flat and easy to follow,
2) explicitly provide an API with get_constexpr in the normal accessor that returns 0

commit message:
Update environment for kesch after system upgrade (#816)

Description: There was a major upgrade of the kesch system. Here we update the environment used for testing with jenkins.

Details:
1) Environment
* set of modules changed: some defaults in kesch are now cuda8, gcc5.3, python3
* A new submit.kesch.perftest.slurm is created to simply increase the time limit of the perf tests submitted to kesch, since some times the tests take longer than 15 mins. 
* build scripts still had the option "-c c++11" which was not used anymore. It was removed from build script, and "-c" reused (see below). 
2) Hacks & Workarounds
* there is currently an issue with performance of communication on CPU (long initialization times) which is affecting the times of mpi unittests. The might timeout. The build script integrates a "-c" option now (without arguments) that is deactivating the CPU MPI communication tests. If there are problems with jenkins timeout, pass that option to the build script in all jenkins plans. Add "-c" (without argument) only in the case some jobs trigger the timeout limit
* The mpi library needs to be passed to linker before the cuda libraries. At the moment we are not controling that order, so we need to add the mvapich mpi library in a LD_PRELOAD in the environment before running tests in kesch. 
3) Plotting
* python scripts were updated to python3
* svg plots did not render anymore in a browser. The code is now plotting png figures

Performance modifications:
Minor performance changes in both cpu and gpu (mainly improvements) due to change of compiler: gcc 4.9 -> 5.3, cuda 7.0 -> cuda 8.0.

author: Mauro Bianco <mbianco@cscs.ch>
commit message:
Fix alignment and storage_info API cleanup (GC-151, #837)

Description: Alignment before this PR was implemented in a non general way. It assumed the memory allocation provided a prescribed alignment (for cuda the value is 256 bytes). This limits the amount of alignment that can be guaranteed. 

Now alignment is specified as before, by indicating that the aligned address (the beginning of the inner region indicated by `halo`) will be multiple of `Align * sizeof(storage_value_type)`. Why alignment is generally specified in bytes and not in `sizeof(value_type)`, changing this would imply that `storage_info` would need to know about the value type of the storage in which it will be used, and this is not our current design.

Additional changes: This PR also cleans up the interface to `storage_info` since some member functions are not needed, and some computations (`m_initial_offset`) is not needed anymore in the `storage_info`.

API changes:
- `storage_info::get_initial_offset()` , `storage_info::begin()` `storage_info::end()`, `storage_info::total_begin()` `storage_info::total_end()` are removed [initial offset would be always `0`, `begin()` and `end()` would not give any indication of the iteration space, and `total_begin()` and `total_end()` are never used to iterate over data, and would iterate over padding and everything else - it was not clear from the api if initial_offset was included, too]
- `storage_info::length`, `storage_info::total_length` and `storage_info::padded_total_length` return the number of elements in the inner region, the inner_region plus halo, and the one including padding, respectively
- `storage_info::length<Dim>`, `storage_info::total_length<Dim>` and `storage_info::padded_length<Dim>` return the number of elements in the specified dimension index `Dim` for inner, outer and padded regions, respectively
- `storage_info::dim`, `storage_info::unaligned_dim`, `storage_info::unaligned_strides` have been removed, since they were ambiguous, redundant and, for the case of unaligned_strides, not clearly defined
- `cuda_storage`, `host_storage`, and `mic_storage` do not have constructors to initialize with a value anymore. There is only one constructor that takes a lambda. `data_store` can still be constructed with a value
- `cuda_storage`, `host_storage`, and `mic_storage` main constructor requires the size, the offset to align (typically the first element of the inner region), and the alignment value, in terms of number of elements of the storage
- I introduced other functions to get storage_info classes with a custom alignment, since I wanted to try them out

Performance changes: No performance changes, because our benchmarks are not sensitive to the changes in this PR.

commit message:
Enable the MPI-based communication tests (GC-48, #445)

Feature description: Enabling the communication tests (MPI-based) for
inclusion in the automatic testing. Fixes #439.

Details:
- Implemented a google-test listener to handle GCL tests as regular
  unit-tests. The listener perform reductions to assess the result of
  the test globally, while each task output stream is redirected to a
  file identified by the task id. The listener also assign GPUs to
  MPI-tasks (works for OSU's MVAPICH2 and CRAY's MPI).
- The halo-update tests and the all-to-all have been transformed into
  unit tests. They have a standalone version that can be compiled
  separately and launched manually. The code of the tests is actually
  in the `example` folder. The halo-update tests also have two targets
  for each source code. The ones terminating with a `_v` test the so
  called vector interface, in which a pattern receives a `std::vector`
  of pointers instead of a comma separated list of pointers (both
  interfaces are used)
- Extensive re-factoring of CMake files to avoid some issues with
  library ordering. One issue is specific to GDR enabled MVAPICH2,
  another in the way `cuda_add_executable` in certain versions of
  CMake deal with `-std=c++11`. For this reason `mpicxx`is not used
  anymore, and CUDA libraries are included manually instead of letting
  `cuda_add_executable` handle them.

Performance Changes: There are no performance changes. I have been
asked to add `-arch=native` as compilation flag, but this has been
moved to a subsequent story. The communication tests are not part of
the performance evaluation at this point, and it's not clear if it
will ever be, since running at scale and getting statistical stability
seems economically unfeasible.

Additional Changes:
- To make the tests passing after a merge, the verifier has been
  updated to make a different estimation of floating point
  approximations base on relative errors only. This is a piggy-backed
  feature that should have been in a separate PR, I guess, but this
  seemed to make the tests to pass with higher probabilities.
- Environments for testing use now different environment variables for
  single node, MPI on host, and MPI on GPUS, and three different job
  files. This has been necessary since MVPICH2 has a problem that
  makes the host tests to hang if the GPU's environment is ON, and
  naturally, GPUs tests fails if host environment is on.

commit message:
k-caches for structured grids (GC-220, #671, #454, #525)

Feature description: Provide an implementation for k-caches. At the moment the implementation is only for the CUDA backend and structured grids. Fixes #454.

Details: the k-cache provides (if specified by the user) a local register ring buffer, private to each thread, that is used to cache values of a field accessed with vertical offsets which are reused at the execution of consecutive vertical planes. The CUDA backend implements functionality to slide the ring buffer everytime the iterators are moved in the vertical dimension, and fill & flush in order to synchronize the cache with the main memory of the gpu. 
        
Performance changes: vertical_advection_dycore is now using k-caches, which improves its performance.

API changes: 
All extents must provide correct values for the k accesses (in order for k caches to properly work). Before the k-extents where not used but could be provided. There is no check that imposes that: this will be done in another task.

Additional changes:
The check that all output parameters have a null extent is relaxed to only the IJ plane, i.e. we allow to write at non-zero offset in k. Fixes #525.

author: Hannes Vogt <hannes@havogt.de>
commit message:
Bugfix: array<T,0> should have size()==0 (GC-316, #824)

Bug description: A gridtools::array<T,0> (zero size) was wrongly setting its size to 1 in many places. E.g. size() returned 1, operator[0] was not protected, iterating from begin() to end() was doing 1 iteration, ...

Fix: Change only the type of the internal storage to have array size = 1, but keep size() == 0 and other protections in place.

Additional changes:
- Remove the public `n_dimensions`. Access to the array size should go via size(), or the newly introduces tuple_size<>, which mimics std::tuple_size<>.
- Remove `dimension::direction` (there was already a duplicated element called `index` with a proposed rename).
- Introduce `position_offset_type` as alias to `array<X,4>` to make it easier to follow its usage. Especially where `is_array<>` was used to do a special calculation.
- In iterate_domain: `set_index()` for scalar type is replaced by `reset_index()` (as it was always used to initialize all elements to zero). `get_index()` -> `index()` and returning array_index_t instead of passing a reference to be filled.
- Move dot product for arrays (via operator*()) from member function to free function in array_addons and enable only for arithmetic types.
- Remove `set_index_recur` which was doing a recursive array copy, comments suggested that this was a performance optimization, but I couldn't see any difference.

commit message:
fix performance (#1611)

With C++17, `as_const` was added into the standard and if `as_const` is not called qualified, we end up with `std::as_const` (which is also a better match) in most cases because there is some `std` inside one of the template arguments.

By qualifying `as_const`, performance is fixed.

For GTBench, performance is identical with `-std=c++14` and `-std=c++17` now.

commit message:
compile time lengths support in data stores (#1545)

The changes is the storage API:
- Data store builder `dimensions` method now accepts both integers and integral constants. Type information is propagated to the data store that is built.
- The properly typed lengths and strides are available to the user via the `native_lengths()` and `native_strides()` methods from data_store/view/info.
- Data store sid adapter uses `native_lengths()`/`native_strides()` now. So the knowledge of the compile time lengths is propagated to the SID API
- call operator of the data store view is now also `compile time aware`. I.e. if the dimension offsets are provided as integral constants and all strides are also known in compile time, no stride computations are performed in run time.  
- There are minor backward incompatibilities to the public API:
  - `data_store` and `info` template classes are moved from the public `gridtools::storage` namespace. They should be considered implementation details now.
  - `lengths()` and `strides()` methods now return by value, not by const reference.

commit message:
Check iteration space fits in the storages (GC-165, #616)

Feature description: Implements a check to ensure the iteration space is small enough to fit in the storages.

Details: Special care has to be taken to avoid "killed dimensions" and lower dimensional arrays (for this reason the `at_<I>()` function is used from the `layout_map` instead of the safer `at<I>()`.
The check expect a separate `grid_traits` to grab the indices of the proper coordinates to be compared, so only one code works for structured and icosahedral grids.

Additional changes:
- Tests have been updated to pass this check and a new unit tests is checking the functionality.
- This PR also fixes a problem with default interval, which was making the check failing. The problem there was a wrong first level placement (due to cut & paste from a wrong example). The first level of a default *axis* should be `(0,-1)` not `(0,-2)`. Also the first level can coincide with the first level of the axis, while the last level of the axis must exceed by at least `1` the top-most level.

commit message:
Bugfix for contains_no_IJ_cache_t (#998)

Description: We compared against an exact type `boost::integral_constant<bool, true>` instead of its contained value. This caused that we wrongly assume that all stencils don't contain IJ caches which implies that we don't do a necessary synchronization. This was fixed already in #993, but the reference was not updated (i.e. performance is worse, but results are fixed; it is a race-condition which we did not catch with our tests). Here we just fix the computation of the contains_no_IJ_cache_t.

Performance changes:
Reference reverted (degradation) to before #988, because the change in reference was due to the incorrect cache behavior introduced in #980, which was again fixed in #993.

commit message:
Improve indexing for temporaries (GC-241, #700)

Feature description: In the iterate domain we are using a pointer and an offset to access a data point. The pointer used in the old indexing approach was the first accessible point of the storage (e.g., halo or data point). In order to be aligned even when using temporaries with different halo accesses in the aligned dimension the halo access information was passed as template information. This information was used to provide aligned data accesses for all temporaries but unfortunately this overhead increased compile times a lot. The new indexing is initializing the pointer to the first aligned data point (non-halo point) and provides aligned accesses for all temporaries without the need of passing plenty of type information across the gridtools internals.

Documentation: The algorithm is explained in detail in the Documentation branch (./docs/internal/new_indexing.md)

Performance changes: None

commit message:
k-axis API (GC-93, GC-133, #753, #568, #444, #433)

# Feature description:
Provides a simpler API to define the vertical axis by introducing an axis types where the number of intervals are passed at compile time, and the sizes of the intervals at run time. The number and size of intervals gives access to an axis_interval and inserts the correct values in the "value_list" when creating a grid from the axis. Fixes #444, fixes #433. Reviews were done on havogt/gridtools#4 and #568.

# API changes:
### Adds a new class "axis<#intervals>" with members
- axis_interval_t: defines an interval which previously was the interval usually called "axis" in the examples and unit_tests, i.e. the template argument of the grid.
- full_interval: defines the interval spanning the full computation domain
- get_interval<Index>: defines the interval corresponding to the Index, where Index < #intervals. Interval sizes correspond to the values passed to the axis ctor.
### Additions to class "interval":
- modify<left, right>: returns an interval which is shrinked/enlarged by the values left and right (within the allowed Offsets for the level).
- shift<dir>: shifts the interval by dir, i.e. calls modify<dir,dir>
### Changes to class "grid":
- new ctor: accept a value_list array as third argument
- mark all other ctors as deprecated as they will construct a partially initialized object (value_list not initialized).
- make_grid(halo_descriptor, halo_descriptor, axis<N>(...)) and make_grid(halo_descriptor, halo_descriptor, int): the first maker is for the general case where you need more than 2 splitters (more than one interval), the axis ctor takes the sizes of the intervals; the second maker is for the simple case of one interval the axis will be automatically deduced to be axis<1>.
### New meta-function join_interval<Intervals...> which will return an interval such that all Intervals are a subset.

# Additional changes:
### Simplify several meta-functions:
- Add "is_all" and "all_" to be used by more specialized ones (all_integrals, etc.)
- Moved "is_all_integral" from variadic_pack_metafunctions.hpp to all_integrals.hpp.
- Renamed "all_integers" to "all_integrals"
### Add a helper for comparing types in unit tests: ASSERT_TYPE_EQ which will produce static assert and print both types (by a compiler error).

No aggregator (GC-324, #888)

Description: Instead of the domain, the make_computation now accepts a  variadic pack of arg_strorage_pair. Placeholders which are not bound in make_computation have to be passed to the run() as arg_storage_pairs.

Details:
- `aggregator_type` is gone;
- instead of `domain` `make_computation` now accepts a variadic pack that consists of `arg_strorage_pair`s and `mss_descriptor`s;

- `computation` type erasure is introduced for  `make_computation` results
- `ready` and `steady` methods of `intermediate` are gone.
- `finalize` is renamed to `sync_all`
- `run` now accepts `arg_storage_pair`s that were not set in `make_computation`.
- `intermediate_expanded` implementation is redone based on new `intermediate` interface

Additional changes:
- `tuple_util` library is introduced
- `meta` library is tuned a bit
- `split_args` utility is introduced

- `fusion.hpp` is gone

commit message:
c_bindings: Allow cross-compilation (GC-538, #1064)

Description: Refactoring of the CMake macro for generating bindings.

API changes:
- Named arguments: add_bindings_library(<library-name> SOURCES <sources>[...] [FORTRAN_OUTPUT_DIR fortran_dir] [C_OUTPUT_DIR c_dir] [FORTRAN_MODULE_NAME name])
- Rename bindings.cmake -> gt_bindings.cmake
- gt_bindings.cmake injects an option to the user's CMake options: `GT_BINDINGS_CROSS_COMPILATION`. If enabled, the bindings will not be regenerated during CMake execution. In this case the bindings should be part of the user's code base.

Details:
The new mechanism will, if GT_BINDINGS_CROSS_COMPILATION=OFF (default):
- generate the bindings as before
- diff the generated bindings against existing bindings
- in case there are no differences, the old ones will be kept (newly generated ones will be deleted), since the old files are not touched, no recompilation of dependencies is trigger as expected
- in case there are differences, the newly generated bindings are kept and a warning is issued, reminding the user to update existing bindings

If GT_BINDINGS_CROSS_COMPILATION=ON:
- no bindings are generated
- if bindings exist, they are used (no diagnostic possible if they are up-to-date).
- if there are no existing bindings, a fatal error message is displayed with the hint to generate bindings first

Additional changes:
Examples and unit_tests are updated to this new pattern: bindings are made part of the repository. Since bindings can change in floating point precision, a separate bindings file needs to be kept for each float and double.

commit message:
Loop Blocking for fn GPU Backend (#1787)

Implements loop blocking for the GPU fn backend. Thread block size (that
is, CUDA/HIP threads per block) and loop block size (that is, loop
iterations per CUDA/HIP thread) can now be specified as template
parameters.

Further changes:
- Set `__launch_bounds__` in the fn GPU kernel based on the thread block
size.
- Activate vertical loop blocking in the fn nabla kernels on newer CUDA
versions that support `GT_PROMISE`.

Performance changes:
- `__launch_bounds__` affects performance of the
`fn_cartesian_vertical_advection` benchmark significantly (positively or
negatively, depending on domain size).
- Performance of fn nabla benchmarks improves significantly on newer
CUDA versions.
- Performance on Daint is currently reduced due to too old CUDA version.

author: Anton Afanasyev <31539054+anstaf@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Introduce functional model backend (#1648)

An API is placed into `gridtools::fn` namespace.
It more or less follows IR specification.
 * vertical stencils are not implemented.
 * only naive execution is implemented.
 * `lift` implemented in two ways: `ilift` (with inlining) and `tlift` (with temporaries).
 * in the case of `tlift` backends internally parses each stencil to AST; transforms that AST to canonical form; generates temporaries and another `fencil` that is actually executed.
 * both Cartesian and unstructured domains are implemented.

commit message:
API change: fix get_interval in k-axis API (GC-338, #854)

Bug description: get_interval<X> and get_interval<X+1> is overlapping.

Solution:
get_interval<X> will return an interval interval<level<X,+1>,level<X+1,-1>>

Details:
Previously the first splitter was placed after the first k-level and the last splitter after the last level which is asymmetric and confusing:
```x|xxxxxxx|```
Now the first splitter is to the left of the first splitter:
```|xxxxxxxx|```
In this example with 8 k-levels the elements of the `value_list` are `{0,8}` while previously it was `{0,7}`. To achieve that the 0 is not moved the `level<0,1>` is associated with `value_list[0]` while previously `level<0,-1>` was associated with `value_list[0]`.

API changes: The previously described re-definition of the `value_list` elements to the `<X,+1>` level is a tiny but very severe change: all users which are still using the old way of defining the k-axis (i.e. not using the get_interval and filling the value_list manually), will have to carefully fix their intervals. Users of the new k-axis API (or the default interval) are not affected by this change.
Therefore, it is recommended to update your code to the k-axis API before using this fix. Because of the bug described above you need to use a work-around: instead of `get_interval<X>` use `get_interval<X>::modify<1,0>` for all `X>1` (not for `X==0`).

Performance: No change.

commit message:
fix performance (#1611)

With C++17, `as_const` was added into the standard and if `as_const` is not called qualified, we end up with `std::as_const` (which is also a better match) in most cases because there is some `std` inside one of the template arguments.

By qualifying `as_const`, performance is fixed.

For GTBench, performance is identical with `-std=c++14` and `-std=c++17` now.

commit message:
Refactoring of the code around gridtools::intermediate (GC-263, #820)

Description: Refactoring of the code around gridtools::intermediate with significant reduction of code size. Added functionality conditionals don't have to be unique types, reduction can be used within conditionals.

Details:
a) Refactoring of conditionals
- the work with gridtools::conditional is encapsulated  within `condition_tree.hpp` now. The interface for conditionals are exposed to the rest of `stencil-computation` via `branch_selector` class.
- as a side effect of this refactoring, conditions are no longer required to be of unique type within `make_computation`.
- one more side effect: reductions can be be placed within conditionals now. The implicit requirement is that reductions in the conditional tree should have common reduction type (strictly speaking `std::common_type` of all reduction type should have `type` defined). 
b) `aggregator_type` no longer contains the fusion set of storage_info pointers. This information is computed on the fly when local_domains are formed.
c) mss args transformations from arg to vector to arg to data_store_filed is moved from `intermediate` to `intermediate_expandable`.
d) all `make_computation` overloads are in the same place now; most of the code from make_computation function is moved to intermediate.
e) some code from backend and backend traits that is used only in intermediate and doesn't depend on backend is moved to intermediate (to be continued in the next PRs).
f) other minor cleanups

Additional changes:
- in `defs.hpp` `GT_AUTO_RETURN` is introduced, which is widely used in this PR.

Implement check for consecutive storage placeholder indices (GC-111, #585, #557)

Bug description: Implement check for consecutive storage placeholder indices. Fixes #557.

commit message:
Add protection against misuse of device namespace (#1581)

This PR protects against a fragile design pattern that I already observed in `gtc` code:
`foo.hpp`:
```c++
void foo() {device::bar();}
```
`baz.cpp`:
```c++
#include "foo.hpp"
int main() {foo();}  // ok
```
`baz.cu`
```c++
#include "foo.hpp"
int main {foo();} // opps
```

commit message:
Store data_store by value in arg_storage_pair (GC-297, #784, #738, #711)

Feature description: Pass `data_store` to`arg_storage_pair` by value. As the members of the data_store are smart pointers the data_store itself acts like a smart pointer. Storing a pointer to the data_store didn't allow to pass around data_stores by value. Fixes #738, fixes #711.

Additional changes:
 - use perfect forwarding when passing `arg_storage_pair`, `aggregator_type` and storage_data`
 - create uninitialised fusion vector of  `arg_storage_pair`s in special way to avoid nvcc warnings
 - fully refactor `intermediate_expand` because the previous implementation used the fact that `arg_storage_pair` contains pointers
- remove assertions from `data_store` copy ctors, assignment operators, and member accessors.
- add some syntax sugar (`==`, `(bool)`) to `data_store` to simplify test code.

commit message:
Remove warnings (GC-142, #1, #565)

Description: GridTools is emitting a lot of compiler warnings, especially in CUDA mode. Fixes #1, fixes #243, fixes #145.

Solution: Since CMake with CUDA does not properly respect the system flag in the include_directories() command, we pass the -isystem explicitly to include the boost libraries. This removes warnings coming from the boost library. Still there were many real warnings left. These warnings were about:
- missing GT_FUNCTION
- GT_FUNCTION where it should not be
- implicit conversion from int to uint
- arithmetic operation on void ptr
- double definition of macros specifying the MPL/Fusion vector sizes (solved by prefixing an undef)
- wrong use of .template
- remove comparison of uint > 0
- const on by-value return type
Some warnings were actually pointing to bugs:
- in include/common/dimension.hpp the value should be int not uint since it specifies an offset
- many of the conversion between signed and unsigned should be fixed in a proper way

commit message:
Stencil functions: remove with_offsets, cleanup default interval (GC-261,#720,#718)

Description: Before, there was a with and and with_offsets, where with ignored the offsets which are specified by the user. This is non-intuitive for the user. Here we rename with_offsets to with (and always respect offsets). Fixes #718.

API change:
- call<...>::with_offsets is removed
- call<>::with which now respects the offsets (former with_offsets)

Additional changes:
- Remove code duplication introduced by the default_interval
- Default interval function calls now allow offsets/at in k. This restriction doesn't make sense if a default_interval functor is called from an interval which is smaller than the default_interval.

commit message:
Fn Frontend (#1698)

Introduces the user-frontend as described in #1674 with the following changes:
- It requires specification and passing of neighbor lookup tables.
- Executors do not automatically execute in the destructor, but require an explicit `.execute()` call.
- There is no `make_tmp_like(…)` function. Instead use `allocate_global_tmp<T>(…)`.
- There is no support for local/blocked temporaries.

commit message:
Bypass extent analysis (GC-245, #727)

Feature description: This update introduces the ability to skip the extent analysis for stencils for which the user had done the extent computation already. The stages are then associated with an extent by calling `make_stage_with_extents<functor, extent>` so that the map between stages and extents to compute temporary sizes is done directly with that information.

Additional information: This is a change the is possible since now all temporaries share the same sizes to reduce register pressure. The map between placeholders and extents are not needed anymore in the backend, otherwise this interface would not work. A future architecture that requires the explicit map for performance, is going to deprecate this approach.

API change: adding `make_stage_with_extents`

commit message:
Resolve race condition when using ij-caches (GC-197, #617)

Description: There is a race condition when using IJ cached fields in combination with multi stage stencils and offsets.

Details: The problem appears because in the last stage there is no syncthreads call but it can be that one warp is consuming values that were produced by another warp. Without synchronization it can happen that the producing warp is already in the next k-level but the old values were not consumed yet.

Performance changes: Fixing this issue introduces an additional syncthreads call after the last ESF. This of course gives a performance penalty. But due to the reason that this synchronization is simply missing we have to fix this and accept the performance loss.

commit message:
Vendor `demangle.hpp` header from Boost (#1816)

This pulls in the `demangle.hpp` header from Boost
(https://github.com/boostorg/core/blob/787b03ea9ca35089cecb80c5f2ca37e10046fbaf/include/boost/core/demangle.hpp)
and moves it into the `gridtools` namespace.

I've done this conversion manually, since it's only one header and it
hasn't changed in the last 9 years in Boost. The dependency on
`boost/config.hpp` in the original version is only for
`BOOST_HAS_PRAGMA_ONCE` (replaced to use `#pragma once`
unconditionally), `BOOST_GCC` (check for `__GNUC__` directly) and
`BOOST_NOEXCEPT` (use `noexcept` unconditionally).

commit message:
New versioning scheme (#1118)

The following will be our new release and versioning scheme:
Version number: X.Y.Z
- X: Major version will be 0 until the public release, then it will be 1, probably until a new major feature, e.g. complete icgrid.
- Y: Minor version will be increased after every API change and new smaller features, probably very often.
- Z: Patch version will be increased for bug fixes.

After each minor release we will make a release branch. The master will then point to the next minor release. In the release branch we can still cherry-pick bugfixes from the master and make a patch release.

The CMake version matching is changed in this release to `COMPATIBILITY SameMinorVersion` which means the following: Let's say the user requires `find_package(GridTools 0.18.2)`. Then `0.18.3` (a newer patch release) will be compatible; `0.18.1` (an older than requested release) and `0.19.0` (a newer minor release) will be rejected.

commit message:
Minor changes to sid (#1548)

- `sid::shifted` and `sid::multi_shifted` helpers are added
- `sid::shift` can also accept now R-value as a pointer. In this case it is a noop.
-  `sid::loop` API is extended to accept `(Ptr&&, Strides const&)` (was only `(Ptr&, Strides const&)` previously). This means that now one can write: `sid::make_loop<dim::i>(size_i)(body)(origin(), strides);` instead of `auto ptr = origin(); sid::make_loop<dim::i>(size_i)(body)(ptr, strides);`. In the first variant the final shift to the initial point will be skipped (techicaly `noop` overload will be used for the final shift).

(https://github.com/boostorg/preprocessor/tree/boost-1.87.0, same as

only the headers from Boost.Preprocessor that gridtools actually uses
(including transitive includes of course). Macros are renamed to
`GT_PP_*` (from `BOOST_PP_*`). The vendored headers are now in
`include/gridtools/preprocessor`. I'm not sure if you want to have them
in some slightly less conspicuous place? Do you consider any `GT_*`
macros to be part of the public API, or is that unspecified (should they
be called `GT_IMPL_PP_*` instead)?

There are 226 vendored headers, compared to 400 in the upstream Boost
version.

commit message:
Distributed boundaries (GC-270, #812)

Feature description: This is a new library in the GridTools. The description can be found in `docs/manuals/user_manual/comm_and_bc.hrst`. The main idea is to combine boundary conditions and communication in a single interface. The API will instantiate the `halo_exchange` pattern and the use is to indicate a list of "jobs", each consisting either of data stores to exchange of boundary condition specifications from which the data stores for communication will be extracted. The interface allows to leave certain data stores out from the communication if they are needed only in boundary conditions or if they are read-only.

commit message:
Fix Clang warning with __builtin_assume (#1788)

Building the project with `Clang` generates the following warning:
```
the argument to '__builtin_assume' has side effects that will be discarded [-Wassume]
```

Seems like Clang doesn't handle the hint well unless we pass a
const/pure attribute to the function call inside the assume. See:
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/55636 and
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/93077

With this change performance for the fn fused nabla examples is
significantly improved on clang-cuda and is now much faster than (our
old) nvcc, which doesn't have `assume` support.

commit message:
CMake refactoring (#1421)

GridTools is now header only (including gcl), this allowed to simplify CMake installations significantly. User should now link to their CMake targets to a specific backend, e.g. `backend_cuda`, `backend_mc`, `storage_mc` etc. Available targets will be listed in the documentation and enabled targets will show during configure of GridTools.

The major changes:
 - `gcl` library is made header only
 - the code within `include/gridtools` is not anymore controlled by explicitly defined macro definitions. I.e. `#if`s and `#ifdefs`style dispatch is made against the compiler predefined macros.        
 -  there is no `GT_SINGLE_PRECISION`, `GT_TESTS_ICOSAHEDRAL_GRID`, `GT_USE_MPI`, `GT_ENABLE_BACKEND_*` CMake options. The only flag that controls the build is `GT_CLANG_CUDA_MODE` (is used to resolve ambiguity between nvcc-clang and clang-cuda). CMake will generate all the build targets it can using the provided C++ compiler and availability of MPI/OpenMP/CUDA/Fortran etc.
 -  previously it was a single `gridtools` target (interface library) that represented all header only stuff what we had. Now `gridtools` is still in place, but represents only backend independent part of the gridtools. In addition to it there are `backend_naive`/`backend_x86`/`backend_mc`/`backend_cuda` libraries for stencil coposition backends; `gcl_cpu`/`gcl_gpu` for communication; `strorage_x86`/`storage_mc`/`storage_cuda` for storages and so on. 
- helpers for enabling CUDA properly on targets: link to a cuda backend, then apply `gridtools_setup_target(tgt)` on a target. This will

commit message:
int_vector library (#1672)

for manipulation of offsets, sizes and extents in `fn` (fixes #1669).

`int_vector` is a `hymap` which value types are all either of integral types or (gridtools) integral constant types with the following functions defined
- `plus`  -- a function that takes two `int_vector`'s and return an `int_vector`. The dimensions (keys) of the result is the the union of the arguments keys. 
- `multiply` -- a function that accepts an `int_vector` and a scalar (integral or integral_constant) and returns an `int_vector`
- `prune_zeros`  -- a function that takes an`int_vector` and removes dimensions which values are equal to `0_c`

author: Alberto Madonna <madonna@cscs.ch>
commit message:
Added automatic stage detection from get_interior_points
functions

In order to use the newly computed ghost cells when generating interior points for the Python backend, get_interior_points() functions have to know which Stage object's ghost cell to pass to the points generator.
To do this, a number of techinques to detect which stage a given call to get_interior_points() corresponds to.
* For a stage defined with a function, the name of the stage can be obtained by looking into the calling stack frame of get_interior_points
* For a stage defined through a for loop in the kernel, the position of the get_interior_points call in the kernel source code is compared to the code stored in the StencilScope and to the line numbers of Stage AST nodes.
* For a stage in a procedural stencil (which uses the static version of get_interior_points), a reference to the Stencil object is obtained by looking at the arguments of the kernel wrapper; after that, a procedure similar to the one used for for-loop-defined stages is applied.

Also added a Stencil function to return a stage given a partial name string.

commit message:
Added explicit setter/getter methods for backend, halo, k direction

The methods are defined as static methods for the Stecil class, as bound methods for MultiStageStencil, and overridden for UserStencil.
They allow to correctly handle the following cases:
- Intending to use global settings for an OOP kernel and not defining stencil data members would have caused the generation of incorrect cpp sources when run with c++ or cuda backend (Jinja templates were directly accesing the halo and k direction object members, having no clue about global Stencil alternatives).
- Setting individual values for a stencil generated from a procedurally defined kernel would have caused the pre-execution checks to verify values that would not be the ones used when running the kernel.
- In general, it should not be possible to define specific settings for a procedural-style stencil. This possibility should be retained for OOP-defined stencils.

commit message:
Added existence checks for missing cases

Most `get...()` functions have `has...()` equivalents (e.g., `getDefSVFGNode()` and `hasDefSVFGNode()`). However, certain getters (e.g., `getLLVMValue()`, `getLHSTopLevelPtr()` had no such existence-checking counterparts. This commit adds a number of these checking functions in cases where they were missing.

Note that these are for cases where the getters fail an assertion when no valid value exists. Cases where the getter simply returns a null-pointer on failure to find any corresponding values (e.g., `ICFG::getFunEntryBlock()`, `ICFG::getFunExitBlock()`, etc.), so a null-check can be used to catch cases where the getter fails to get any corresponding object, and thus don't need a corresponding existence checker.
